title: How to use voice typing in Google Docs on Mac: a step by step guide
metaTitle: How to Use Voice Typing in Google Docs on Mac
description: Learn how to use voice typing in Google Docs on Mac: open Tools, click the mic, say punctuation, and fix common microphone problems in your browser.
targetKeyword: how to use voice typing in google docs on mac
secondaryKeywords: google docs voice typing not working mac
intro: On a Mac, open a Google Doc in Chrome, Edge or Safari, then choose Tools > Voice typing. Click the microphone to start and click it again to stop, or press ⌘ ⇧ S in Chrome to start.
tldr: Open a Google Doc in Chrome, Edge or Safari, then choose Tools > Voice typing.
Click the microphone to start, and click it again to stop.
In Chrome, press ⌘ ⇧ S to start voice typing, as Google's shortcut list shows.
Allow your browser under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone.
Voice commands work only in English, for both the account and the document.

blocks.text: What you need before you start

You need a Mac with a working microphone and one of three browsers. Google's help page for voice typing says the feature works with the latest versions of Chrome, Edge and Safari. Firefox is not on that list, so use one of the three. Google does not give a minimum macOS version on that page, so keep your Mac and browser updated.

items: A Mac with a built-in microphone, or a headset that is plugged in
Chrome, Edge or Safari, updated to the latest version
A Google Doc you can edit
English as your account language and your document language
Microphone access for your browser in System Settings

blocks.text: The language rule matters most. Google says voice commands work only in English. Your Google account language and your document language must both be English. If either one is not, commands like Stop listening will not work.

Google also warns that punctuation words might not be available in every language. Dictate one test sentence with a comma and a period before you start a long page. That quick test shows whether the setup works before you invest time in a draft.
Which browser to use with voice typing
Google's help pages name the browsers, but they do not give the same details for each one. The table shows what Google states for Chrome, Edge and Safari on the Mac.

blocks.caption: What Google's help pages state for each browser on Mac.

blocks.text: Chrome is the safest choice for the shortcut, because Google labels the shortcut for Chrome browsers. If you use Safari or Edge, start with the Tools menu instead. Google does not say the shortcut works in Safari or Edge.
Allow your browser to use the microphone

Your Mac blocks apps from using the microphone until you allow it. Apple's control guide lets you turn microphone access on or off for each app. Open the Apple menu, choose System Settings, then go to Privacy & Security. Scroll down if needed, and click Microphone.

Find your browser in the list and turn it on. Apple's guide does not name Chrome, and it does not say whether you need to restart. So check the switch first, then try voice typing. If your browser is missing from the list, quit it, open it again, and check the list once more.

Apple's guide is labeled macOS 27, so older versions may show different names. Google's own page also uses two names for the Mac settings. It says System Settings in one place and System Preferences in another. Look for the Microphone item under privacy controls, whatever the window is called.
Start voice typing from the Tools menu
This is the first path Google describes, and it is the easiest to follow. Open your document, click where you want the text to start, then go to Tools > Voice typing.

When the option is open, click the microphone when you are ready to speak. Speak at a normal pace, in full sentences. Click the microphone again when you are done. Google's steps are short, so the whole process takes only a few clicks.
Your words appear where the cursor sits. If you click somewhere else, the next words go there. Keep the cursor where you want the text, and check the result after each short run.
Start voice typing with the keyboard shortcut
Google lists ⌘ ⇧ S as the Mac shortcut for starting voice typing. Google labels it as available in Chrome browsers. Put the cursor in the document, press the shortcut, then speak.
Watch out for ⌘ S. On a Mac, ⌘ S is the save shortcut in Google Docs. ⌘ ⇧ S starts voice typing. The Shift key is the only difference, so look at the keys before you press them.
Say punctuation and new lines out loud

Google calls these punctuation commands. Say Period for a full stop, or Comma for a comma. Other commands include Exclamation point, Question mark, New line and New paragraph. Google warns that some of these might not work in every language.

Pause for a moment before and after each command. That makes it easier to see where a sentence ends, and it helps you catch a command that did not register. Check the text on screen before you keep going.

Here is a short example. Say this: Thanks for the draft comma I will review it tonight period New paragraph Next, the budget numbers. The text you should see is: Thanks for the draft, I will review it tonight. Then a new paragraph begins with Next, the budget numbers.

Use New line for a break inside one paragraph, such as an address or a sign-off. Use New paragraph when you start a new idea. Pick the right one before you speak, because a wrong break is quick to miss.
Stop, resume and finish a session
Say Stop listening to stop voice typing. Say Resume to start again. Google says Resume continues at the end of the paragraph, so it does not return you to the spot where you last clicked.

Say Stop listening before you check a source, read a note aloud, or answer a message. Otherwise the words you read can end up in your document. Resume afterward, then check that the text landed where you meant.
When you finish, click the microphone once more. Then read the section from the top. Small errors are easy to skip while you speak, and they are much easier to catch on a quiet read-through.
Edit dictated text without losing your place
Voice typing is fast for a first draft. Editing takes a separate pass. Dictate one section, stop listening, then read it on screen. Fix names, numbers and dates before you move on.

To fix a word in the middle, click at the spot and type the correction by hand. Then move the cursor back to the end of your text. Resume continues at the end of the paragraph, so the cursor position matters before you dictate again.
Keep a list of names and terms you dictate often. Search for each one before you finish. One check catches every copy of the same error, which is faster than reading every line twice.
Fix voice typing when it does not work

Google's troubleshooting section groups problems into three kinds. They are trouble hearing you, a microphone that does not work, and voice commands that do not work. Start with the one that matches what you see on screen.

items: Trouble hearing you: check that the microphone is plugged in and that no other app is using it.
Microphone not working: quit other apps that use the mic, such as a video call or a recording app, then try again.
Voice commands not working: check that the account language and the document language are both English.
Browser blocked: open System Settings, go to Privacy & Security > Microphone, and turn on your browser.
Wrong input device: check which microphone your Mac is using, especially with a headset or earbuds connected.
Feature turned off: if you use a work or school account, an admin may have disabled voice typing. Ask your admin.

blocks.text: Restart the browser after you change a setting. Apple's guide does not say a restart is needed, so treat this as a precaution, not a rule. If the problem continues, try one of the other two browsers Google lists.

Keep your test simple while you troubleshoot. Dictate one plain sentence with no commands. If that works, the microphone and browser are fine, and the problem sits with a command or a language setting.
Common mistakes people make with voice typing

items: Pressing ⌘ S when they meant ⌘ ⇧ S. Save and voice typing are different shortcuts.
Expecting voice commands in another language. Commands work only in English.
Clicking away in the middle of a paragraph, then saying Resume. Resume returns to the end of the paragraph.
Dictating while a call or recording app holds the microphone. Google's troubleshooting names this as a common cause.
Expecting voice commands in Slides speaker notes. Google says they are not available there.
Reading a source aloud with voice typing still on. Say Stop listening first.

blocks.text: Check the first sentence before you keep going. A wrong setting usually shows up there. It is faster to fix it at the start than at the end of a long page.
Voice typing versus macOS Dictation
macOS has its own Dictation feature, and people mix the two up. Apple's guide puts it under System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation. Turn it on there, then click Enable if your Mac asks you to.
Apple's guide does not name a default shortcut. The shortcut can be changed in the same pane, through the Shortcut pop-up menu. Set your own key if you want one.

The two tools do different jobs. Google voice typing runs in the browser inside Google Docs, and its commands work only in English. macOS Dictation is set up in Apple's settings and is a separate system. Choose the one that fits the task in front of you.
Tips for longer documents
A long report takes several sessions. Put a short outline at the top of the document. Dictate one heading at a time, so you can find your place quickly when you come back.
Make a copy of the file before a long session. Then the original stays clean if a dictation run goes wrong. Give the copy a clear name with the date in it.
Plan for breaks. A short run followed by a read-through is easier to manage than one long session. Long sessions feel fast at first, but the fixes pile up at the end and take longer than you expect.
If the steps above fail, go back to microphone access first. Most setup problems start there, and the Microphone list under Privacy & Security is the first place to check.

faq.question: Does voice typing work in Google Docs on Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. Google's help page describes voice typing as a browser feature for Chrome, Edge and Safari. The help page I checked does not describe a separate Google Docs app for Mac, so open the document in your browser.

faq.question: What is the shortcut for voice typing in Google Docs on Mac?
faq.answer: Google lists ⌘ ⇧ S as the shortcut to start voice typing. Google labels it as available in Chrome browsers, so try it in Chrome first. On a Mac, ⌘ S is the save shortcut, which is a different key combination.

faq.question: Why is the microphone not working in Google Docs?
faq.answer: Check that your browser can use the microphone in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone. Then check that no other app is holding the mic and that the right input device is selected.

faq.question: Can I use voice typing in a language other than English?
faq.answer: Voice commands work only in English. Google says your account language and your document language must both be English. Google also warns that punctuation words might not be available in every language.

faq.question: How do I stop voice typing in Google Docs?
faq.answer: Click the microphone again, or say Stop listening. To start again, say Resume. Google says Resume continues at the end of the paragraph, so check where your cursor is before you speak.

faq.question: Does Google voice typing work in Slides speaker notes?
faq.answer: Google says voice commands are not available in Slides speaker notes. This page covers Google Docs only, so test the feature in a document before you rely on it for anything else.

faq.question: Do I need to restart my Mac after I allow the microphone?
faq.answer: Apple's microphone guide does not say whether a restart is needed. Try voice typing again first. If it still fails, quit the browser, open it again, and check the microphone list once more.

faq.question: Is macOS Dictation the same as Google voice typing?
faq.answer: No. macOS Dictation is set up in System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation. Google voice typing runs in the browser inside Google Docs, and Google controls the speech-to-text service it uses.

steps.name: Allow the microphone for your browser
steps.text: Open the Apple menu and choose System Settings. Go to Privacy & Security, scroll if needed, and click Microphone. Turn on access for your browser in the list.
steps.tip: Apple's guide is labeled macOS 27. Older versions may show slightly different names.

steps.name: Open the Google Doc in a supported browser
steps.text: Open Chrome, Edge or Safari, then open the document. Check that your account and document language are English. Click where you want the text to start.
steps.tip: Google's help page does not list Firefox, so use one of the three.

steps.name: Open the Voice typing command
steps.text: Click Tools in the menu bar at the top of the window. Then click Voice typing. Google's steps start from this menu, so it is the safest first try.
steps.tip: Do this step before you speak, so you know the feature is on.

steps.name: Click the microphone and speak
steps.text: Click the microphone when you are ready to speak. Talk at a normal pace, in full sentences. Say punctuation words out loud when you need them.
steps.tip: Test one sentence first. Punctuation words might not work in every language.

steps.name: Start with the keyboard shortcut instead
steps.text: Put the cursor in the document and press ⌘ ⇧ S. Google lists this shortcut for starting voice typing in Chrome browsers. Then speak.
steps.tip: On a Mac, ⌘ S saves. Check the Shift key before you press.

steps.name: Say the punctuation commands
steps.text: Say Period, Comma, Exclamation point, Question mark, New line or New paragraph. Each one works as a command, so pause briefly before and after it.
steps.tip: Commands work only in English, so keep the document and account in English.

steps.name: Stop or resume
steps.text: Say Stop listening to stop voice typing. Say Resume to continue. Resume carries on at the end of the paragraph.
steps.tip: Say Stop listening before you check a source or read a note aloud.

steps.name: Finish and check the text
steps.text: Click the microphone again when you are done. Read the section from the top. Check names, numbers and dates before you share the document.
steps.tip: Search for a misspelled name once to catch every copy of it.

troubleshooting.problem: We are having trouble hearing you
troubleshooting.fix: Check that the microphone is plugged in and that no other app is using it. Google's troubleshooting section gives these two checks first.
Quit other apps that use the microphone, such as a video call or recording app, then try again. Then check Apple menu > System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone.
Check that your account language and document language are both English. Commands such as Stop listening and Resume will not work in another language.

troubleshooting.problem: Your browser has no microphone access
troubleshooting.fix: Turn on your browser in the Microphone list under Privacy & Security. Quit the browser and open it again if it still does not start listening.

troubleshooting.problem: The wrong microphone is in use
troubleshooting.fix: Check which microphone your Mac is using. A connected headset or earbuds can be picked by mistake, so unplug the device you do not want and test again.

troubleshooting.problem: Voice typing is missing or turned off
troubleshooting.fix: If you use a work or school account, an admin may have disabled voice typing. Ask your admin to check the setting for your account.
